summary.intent: Bootstrap release-please with correct version tags after phase 41 setup, align api-client versions with the API, expose the API version on the /health endpoint, and fix the post-merge release workflow to avoid pushing directly to branch-protected main.
summary.outcome: All 15 bootstrap tags created, api-client versions aligned to 0.35.0, /health endpoint now returns version field, post-merge workflow replaced with PR-time release-as injection, and openapi.json extra-files config corrected for the api-client package.

repo: Release-please was just set up in phase 41 with no prior tags, causing it to treat the entire commit history as unreleased — bootstrap tags fix this.
Phase 41 discussion log explicitly decided monotonic (major.minor) versioning for web and desktop apps, but the implementation used semver for all packages. User accepted semver for now.

The OpenAPI spec generation script manually defines the /health endpoint (instead of using HealthController) because HealthController depends on TypeOrmHealthIndicator which requires a real DB connection.

release-please extra-files paths are resolved relative to the package directory, so a file at packages/api-client/openapi.json must be listed under that package's config (not apps/api), otherwise the path resolves to a nonexistent location.

The post-merge release workflow was designed to push release-as targets directly to main, but branch protection with required status checks blocks github-actions[bot] even with bypass settings toggled.
PR release preview labels were picking up merge commits as real changes, generating false bump labels across many packages.
The GITHUB_TOKEN cannot trigger new workflow runs on push (GitHub's built-in recursion prevention), making it safe to commit back to PR branches from CI.

code.finding: OpenAPI version was hardcoded as 0.1.0; changed to read from npm_package_version with fallback to reading package.json via fs.
Same hardcoded 0.1.0 version issue; fixed to fail-fast if env var missing.
New shared module extracted to deduplicate version-reading logic used in both main.ts and health.controller.ts.
Health controller now returns version field sourced from shared API_VERSION constant; response shape is { status, info, error, details, version }.
Merge commits (2+ parents) were being parsed as conventional commits, generating false release labels; fixed by filtering on parents length.
Manual label overrides (existing higher-or-equal labels) were not being fed back into packageBumps, causing release-as targets to use computed (lower) bump instead of the manual override.
Clearing stale release-as entries needed to snapshot base branch config first to avoid wiping entries from previously merged PRs.
openapi.json extra-files entry must be on packages/api-client (where the file lives), not apps/api; paths are resolved relative to package directory.

workflow: fix: commit type triggers release-please patch bumps; use chore(ci): for CI-only changes that should not affect versioning.
Squashing multiple commits into one chore(ci): commit before pushing prevents cascading version bump labels from release-please.
Bootstrap tags should be created on the commit just before the first release-please setup commit so the first release PR only includes intended changes.
Branch protection legacy rules don't support per-actor bypass; rulesets do but had prior issues — workaround was removing the post-merge push entirely.
PR review comments from Copilot and CodeRabbit should be verified against current code before applying — some may already be addressed or not applicable.
When rebasing a branch that touches the same files as a recently merged PR, it's faster to recreate the branch from current main than to resolve conflicts.

friction: Branch protection blocked the post-merge workflow from pushing to main even with 'Do not allow bypassing' unchecked — required a full architecture change to move release-as injection to PR-time.
Legacy branch protection rules don't have the 'Allow specified actors to bypass' option that newer rulesets have, making the original approach unworkable.
Cargo.lock regeneration pulled in unrelated dependency updates when only the crate version needed changing; required manual targeted update.
The git index.lock file was left behind by a crashed git process, blocking subsequent git operations.
PR #432 initially had a huge diff because the branch was created before PR #431 merged — required recreating from current main.
release-please did not bump openapi.json despite the extra-files config because the path was relative to apps/api/ and resolved to a nonexistent location.
A background task notification about a failed commit surfaced after the issue was already manually resolved, causing confusion.
Web E2E was skipped on PR #431 (CI-only changes) causing the Verify E2E Passed gate on the release PR to fall back to an older failed run.
open_items: PR #430 (release PR) still needs Verify API Spec & Client and Verify E2E Passed checks to pass after the openapi.json extra-files fix merges.
The web/desktop apps use semver instead of the originally discussed monotonic (major.minor) versioning — deferred, acceptable for now.
The 'Verify E2E Passed' gate logic falls back to previous runs when E2E is skipped — could produce false failures from unrelated flaky runs; worth revisiting the fallback logic.
Need to confirm that the api-client extra-files jsonpath config for openapi.json actually works when release-please next runs, since the ../../ path approach broke release-please.
